title: 26 CFR 301.7216-2 Permissible disclosures without consent (current through 2026-11-18)
claim: Disclosure of tax return information to an officer, employee or member of the SAME preparer located outside the US requires the taxpayer's prior 7216-3 consent; US-to-US preparer-to-preparer auxiliary disclosures need no consent if no substantive determinations.
excerpt: If an officer, employee, or member to whom the tax return information is to be disclosed is located outside of the United States... consent... is required.
limitations: Federal rule only; state confidentiality rules (e.g., Illinois) not reviewed.

title: 26 CFR 301.7216-3 Disclosure or use permitted only with taxpayer consent
claim: US preparer may not obtain consent to disclose a 1040-series filer's SSN to a preparer outside the US unless both maintain an adequate data protection safeguard (per IRB guidance) and verify it in the consent; consents default to one year; use and disclosure need separate documents; taxpayer gets a copy.
excerpt: may not obtain consent to disclose the taxpayer's social security number (SSN)... to a tax return preparer located outside of the United States
limitations: SSN exception detailed in Rev. Proc. 2013-14.

title: 26 CFR 301.7216-1 Penalty for disclosure or use of tax return information
claim: 'Tax return preparer' includes persons providing auxiliary services and any employee who assists; s.7216 is a misdemeanor (up to 1 year and/or $1,000); s.6713 civil penalty $250 per prohibited disclosure, max $10,000 per calendar year.
excerpt: The penalty for violating section 6713 is $250 for each prohibited disclosure or use, not to exceed a total of $10,000
limitations: The offshore staffing company and each worker are themselves 'tax return preparers' for 7216 purposes (analyst reading of (b)(2)(i)(A)-(D)).

title: Rev. Proc. 2013-14, section 5.07 and mandatory SSN statement
claim: An 'adequate data protection safeguard' is a management-approved security program conforming to a listed framework (e.g., financial-industry standard such as Shared Assessments, AICPA/CICA Privacy Framework, IRS Pub 1075, or an equivalent); offshore-SSN consents must carry a prescribed statement that US agencies may not be able to enforce privacy law abroad.
excerpt: An adequate data protection safeguard is a management-approved and implemented security program, policy, and practice
limitations: Frameworks list dated (Safe Harbor is defunct); 'equivalent' frameworks (e.g., ISO 27001/SOC 2) are analyst reading - confirm with tax counsel.

title: 16 CFR Part 314 (Safeguards Rule) - 314.2(h)(2)(viii), 314.4(c)(3),(c)(5),(f),(j), 314.6
claim: Accountants/tax preparation services are 'financial institutions'; must encrypt customer information in transit and at rest, use MFA for anyone accessing systems, oversee service providers by contract and periodic assessment, and notify the FTC within 30 days of a notification event involving >=500 consumers; firms with <5,000 consumers are exempt only from 314.4(b)(1),(d)(2),(h),(i) - not from vendor oversight.
excerpt: An accountant or other tax preparation service that is in the business of completing income tax returns is a financial institution
limitations: Applies to the CPA firm; the staffing company is its service provider and inherits contract obligations.

title: Publication 4557 Safeguarding Taxpayer Data (Rev. 6-2024)
claim: Under the FTC Safeguards Rule tax return preparers must create and enact written security plans (see Pub 5708 WISP template); failure may result in an FTC investigation; also select capable service providers and require safeguards by contract.
excerpt: tax return preparers must create and enact security plans to protect client data. See Publication 5708
limitations: Guidance publication; legal duty sits in 16 CFR 314.

title: PTIN requirements for tax return preparers (page updated 2026-10-29)
claim: Anyone who prepares or assists in preparing federal tax returns for compensation must have a valid 2027 PTIN; fee $18.75 (new or renewal); 2027 applications being processed.
excerpt: Anyone who prepares or assists in preparing federal tax returns for compensation must have a valid 2027 PTIN
limitations: Foreign preparers without SSN need the supplemental foreign-person form (not fetched); whether a supervised offshore assistant needs a PTIN depends on 'all or substantially all' facts - confirm.

title: Instructions for Forms 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC (Rev. December 2026)
claim: Form 1099-NEC is for nonemployee fees of at least $2,000 to US payees; payments to nonresident aliens use Form 1042-S only for US-source income subject to withholding.
excerpt: Use Form 1042-S, Foreign Person's U.S. Source Income Subject to Withholding, for payments to nonresident aliens.
limitations: Read with Pub 515 (DG-S011): services performed abroad = foreign-source, not wages, not withheld.

title: Instructions for Form W-8BEN
claim: A foreign individual provides Form W-8BEN to establish non-US status and claim exemption from domestic information reporting and backup withholding; foreign entities use W-8BEN-E.
excerpt: Establish that you are not a U.S. person
limitations: Collect from every Philippine contractor; not needed for employees of an own PH entity.

organization: AICPA (copy hosted by Minnesota Board of Accountancy)
title: AICPA Code of Professional Conduct - ET 1.150.040, 1.300.040, 1.700.040 (Use of / Disclosing information to a Third-Party Service Provider)
claim: Before disclosing confidential client information to a TPSP the member should inform the client, preferably in writing (not required for administrative services); must ensure TPSP qualifications and adequately plan and supervise its work; and must either have a confidentiality contract with reasonable assurance of procedures OR obtain specific client consent.
excerpt: before disclosing confidential client information to a third-party service provider, the member should inform the client, preferably in writing
limitations: Professional standard binding AICPA members/state boards that adopt it; Illinois board adoption not verified.

title: United States - Philippines Income Tax Convention (1976), Article 5 Permanent Establishment
claim: PE includes the furnishing of services, including consultancy, by a resident of one State through employees or other personnel where such activities continue in the other State for periods aggregating more than 183 days (same or connected project); control of/by a local subsidiary does not by itself create a PE (Art. 5(8)).
excerpt: The furnishing of services, including consultancy services, by a resident of one of the Contracting States through employees or other personnel
limitations: Application to a US company using full-time Philippine contractors is an analyst reading; BIR practice not verified - Philippine tax counsel must confirm.

title: Presidential Decree No. 851 and implementing rules (13th-month pay)
claim: 13th-month pay = one-twelfth of basic salary within a calendar year, payable not later than 24 December.
excerpt: Thirteenth-month pay shall mean one twelfth (1/12) of the basic salary of an employee within a calendar year
limitations: Original P1,000 salary ceiling was later removed (Memorandum Order No. 28, 1986 - not fetched); verify current DOLE guidelines.

title: Labor Code (PD 442 as amended) - Arts. 86, 94, 95, 106, 280, 283 (pre-renumbering)
claim: Night-shift differential >=10% for each hour 10pm-6am; holiday work paid at twice the regular rate; 5-day service incentive leave after one year; principal jointly liable with contractor for unpaid wages; employment is regular when work is usually necessary or desirable to the business; separation pay of >=1 month per year of service for redundancy or installation of labor-saving devices, with 1 month written notice to worker and DOLE.
excerpt: Every employee shall be paid a night shift differential of not less than ten percent (10%) of his regular wage
limitations: Article numbers were renumbered in 2015 (e.g., 280->295, 283->298); text from LawPhil, not the official gazette.

organization: Supreme Court of the Philippines (via LawPhil)
title: Sonza v. ABS-CBN Broadcasting Corp., G.R. No. 138051 (10 June 2004)
claim: Employer-employee relationship is determined by the four-fold test (selection/engagement, payment of wages, power of dismissal, control of means and methods); the control test is the most important element.
excerpt: The last element, the so-called 'control test', is the most important element.
limitations: Classic case; later cases refine; full-time dedicated seats directed by a CPA firm resemble employment - analyst reading.

title: SSS implements revised contribution rates for 2025
claim: SSS contribution 15% from 1 Jan 2025: employer 10%, employee 5%; monthly salary credit PHP 5,000-35,000 (SSS Circular 2024-006 dated 19 Dec 2024).
excerpt: Total contribution rate 15%; employer 10%; maximum MSC Php35,000 (paraphrase)
limitations: Secondary summary of the official circular (corroborated by KPMG/Vialto search extracts); EC contribution (~PHP 30) not stated - E.

title: PhilHealth Advisory No. 2025-0002 Premium Contribution for All Direct Contributors CY 2025
claim: Premium rate 5.0% of monthly basic salary with floor PHP 10,000 and ceiling PHP 100,000 (PHP 500-5,000/month); computed on basic salary excluding 13th month/allowances; shared between employer and employee (equal split per Circular 2020-0005).
excerpt: the premium rate effective the applicable period of January 2025 remains at 5.0%, with an income floor of P10,000 and income ceiling of P100,000
limitations: 2026 rate not separately verified; equal split is per the referenced circular (not re-read).

title: Republic Act No. 11647 (2022) amending the Foreign Investments Act (RA 7042)
claim: Foreign investment in export enterprises (not on negative lists A/B) allowed up to 100%; non-Philippine-national export enterprises register with BOI and must keep >=60% export ratio; domestic-market enterprises below US$200,000 paid-in capital reserved to Filipinos (US$100,000 if advanced tech, endorsed startup, or majority-Filipino workforce of >=15).
excerpt: Foreign investment in export enterprise... is allowed up to one hundred percent (100%) ownership.
limitations: Minimum capital for an export-services corporation under the Revised Corporation Code not verified; SEC/BOI process and fees MISSING - Philippine counsel.

title: Republic Act No. 10173 Data Privacy Act of 2012, Sec. 4 Scope
claim: The Act does not apply to personal information originally collected from residents of foreign jurisdictions in accordance with their laws, being processed in the Philippines (outsourcing exemption) - but it does apply to the Philippine entity's own employee data.
excerpt: Personal information originally collected from residents of foreign jurisdictions in accordance with the laws of those foreign jurisdictions... being processed in the Philippines
limitations: Exemption scope per NPC rules not reviewed; security obligations still flow from US contracts (7216, Safeguards).

title: Treasury Reporting Rates of Exchange - Philippines peso, India rupee
excerpt: exchange_rate 62.658, record_date 2026-09-30 (API field)
limitations: Quarterly reporting rates, not market rates; PHP weakened ~11% in 15 months, which flatters USD margins on PHP salaries but is not guaranteed.

title: Best offshore staffing companies for accounting firms in 2026 - 18 reviewed by hiring model
claim: Published prices compiled: Penbrothers PEO example $1,463 pay + $500 management fee = $1,963/month, $300 setup, one-month salary deposit; Sourcefit accounting $1,260/$2,010/$2,760 (entry/mid/expert), $0 setup, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type 1; Accountant Offshore ~$2,000 all-in for US accountant ($1,400 + $600 fee), tax preparer $2,900, auditor $3,000; MYCPE ONE from $11/hour; Finsmart $2,400 bookkeeping seat, $3,200 senior, 3-month notice; CapActix billed fortnightly in advance; Vintti LatAm staff accountant ~$1,650/month; 8 of 18 publish no price (incl. TOA Global).
excerpt: Penbrothers example: $1,463 pay plus $500 management fee = $1,963/mo (paraphrase)
limitations: Competitor-authored roundup; figures not all verified at source (Sourcefit 403, Penbrothers pricing page 404 on 2026-11-28).

title: Accounting & bookkeeping outsourcing pricing (USA)
claim: Dedicated resources $2,500/month for staff accountant, tax preparer, bookkeeper, payroll, AR/AP; senior accountant $4,000/month; claims 500+ CPA firms served; SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001/27701; delivery centres in India and Guadalajara, Mexico.
excerpt: Staff Accountant $2,500 monthly; Senior Accountant $4,000 (paraphrase)
limitations: List prices; discounts, minimums and worker cost undisclosed.

title: Pricing
claim: Dedicated staff starting at $2,700/month (bookkeepers & accountants), $2,900 (tax accountants), $3,100 (auditors), $2,200 (virtual assistants); one-time kickoff fee $2,250 covering search, sourcing and equipment setup.
excerpt: one-time kickoff fee of $2,250, which covers search, sourcing, and equipment setup
limitations: 'Starting at' prices; term (one-year per Vintti) not verified on page.

title: Homepage re-check (Stage E)
claim: Talent cost from $1,400 (US accountant), $2,300 (tax preparer), $2,400 (auditor) plus a fixed management support fee covering recruitment, managed equipment, office support, IT, payroll and benefits administration; fee amount not on homepage; no SOC 2/ISO/7216 claims; client case: 15-person team for one US CPA firm.
excerpt: Starting talent cost; fixed management support fee is separate
limitations: Fee ~$600 reported only by Vintti (D, E-WS12012-S020).

title: Occupational Outlook Handbook: Bookkeeping, Accounting, and Auditing Clerks
claim: Employment 1,532,400 (2025), projected -6% (-85,600) 2025-35; median pay $50,670 (May 2025); ~144,100 openings/yr from replacement; decline attributed to software automation.
excerpt: Software innovations have automated many of the tasks performed by bookkeeping, accounting, and auditing clerks.
limitations: US occupation projection; not offshore seats; government statistic (C under Atlas hierarchy).

title: CCH Axcess Adds Agentic AI for Tax Preparation
claim: For Form 1040 the CCH Axcess agents identify and classify source documents, extract and map data into the return, calculate, surface diagnostics and generate workpapers; professionals review and approve; availability/pricing not stated.
excerpt: Expert AI agents prepare, check and advance the work. Professionals review, decide and approve.
limitations: Vendor-announced capability; no measured time savings; business returns not mentioned.

title: Black Ore Launches Tax Autopilot for Broad Availability
claim: Black Ore claims >98% autonomy and up to 80% lower cost per return from an early-access program of 75 firms (waitlist >3,700); presents the product as an alternative to offshore outsourcing for staffing gaps.
excerpt: Tax Autopilot executes the full lifecycle of a complex tax return autonomously
limitations: Vendor claims (D-quality) relayed by trade press; not independently verified.

title: Introducing Ready to Review - agentic AI for 1040 preparation
claim: Thomson Reuters launched agentic AI (Gather and Tax Preparer agents) embedded in the 1040 workflow; its 2026 State of Tax Professionals report says only 11% of firms use no automation (18% in 2025).
excerpt: Ready to Review... agentic AI for 1040 preparation (title)
limitations: Seen through search summary only; page not fetched.

organization: CPA Practice Advisor / Intuit (via search-result summary)
title: Intuit Rolls Out AI Agents for QuickBooks
claim: QuickBooks Accounting Agent automates transaction categorization and assists reconciliation; Intuit-commissioned survey claims 45% of customers save 12 hours/month on bookkeeping with the AI bank feed.
excerpt: 45% of customers save 12 hours each month (paraphrase of Intuit claim)
limitations: Vendor survey; search summary only.

title: Offshoring for CPA firms: The hows and whys
claim: 2023 AICPA MAP survey (>1,100 firms): ~30% outsource domestically, 25% offshore; 14% and 12% plan to start; case: a five-person Atlanta tax firm moved from an India vendor (after vendor turnover) to its own EOR team of nine; AICPA & CIMA publish offshoring tools.
excerpt: about 30% said they outsourced domestically and 25% said they outsourced to offshore workers
limitations: Survey respondents self-selected; case is anecdotal.

title: 2025 AICPA/CIMA PCPS-CPA.com National MAP Survey coverage
claim: 29% of responding firms leverage offshoring, 46% of 'top performing' firms; 15% of firms plan to outsource outside the US in 2026 (Year Ahead survey).
excerpt: 29% of the responding firms leverage offshoring (search extract)
limitations: Figures from search extracts; article body not captured on fetch.

title: About Form 5471 (page updated 2026-09-17)
claim: Certain US citizens/residents who are officers, directors or shareholders of certain foreign corporations must file Form 5471 (IRC 6038/6046) - applies once the founder owns a Philippine subsidiary.
excerpt: Certain U.S. citizens and residents who are officers, directors, or shareholders in certain foreign corporations file Form 5471
limitations: CFC income inclusion and penalty rules not reviewed; international tax CPA needed.

title: Staff accountant salaries in the Philippines
claim: Local Philippine pay: entry-level staff accountant ~PHP 137,739/yr; staff accountant ~PHP 240,000/yr; senior staff accountant ~PHP 290,000/yr - i.e., US-facing offshore pay of ~$1,100/month (~PHP 69,000) is ~3x local staff-accountant pay.
excerpt: ₱240,000 average (staff accountant, search summary)
limitations: Self-reported; not US-tax roles; search summary only.

organization: Pag-IBIG Fund (HDMF) - circular copy hosted by Grant Thornton PH
title: HDMF Circular No. 460: increase in Maximum Fund Salary effective February 2024
claim: Contribution 2% employee and 2% employer for fund salary over PHP 1,500, computed on a maximum fund salary of PHP 10,000 (i.e., max PHP 200 each per month).
excerpt: Over P1,500 2.0% 2.0% (contribution rate table)
limitations: Copy hosted by an accounting firm; official HDMF site not fetched.
